headline: Modi hosts Nepal’s Balendra Shah for trade and connectivity talks
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah at Hyderabad House in New Delhi on Monday to review bilateral trade, investment, energy, and connectivity. Accompanied by a 34-member delegation, Shah’s two-day State visit features a business forum and planned agreements across health, education, and agriculture.
why_it_matters: Deepening commercial, energy, and transport links during Shah’s State visit aims to boost cross-border projects and attract Indian investment into Nepal.
source_search: Modi hosts Nepal’s Balendra Shah for trade and connectivity talks The Hindu

headline: Ukrainian naval drones sink Russian warship off Libya’s coast
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that seven naval drones sank Russia’s corvette Merkury and destroyed a combat helicopter at Benghazi port, Libya, on Sunday. Ukraine also struck the cargo ship MV Angara. Satellite imagery confirmed the warship capsized, prompting UN warnings against exporting foreign conflicts to Libya.
why_it_matters: Striking a Russian warship inside a Libyan port shows Ukraine’s expanding drone reach and risks pulling divided Libya into an external war.
source_search: Ukrainian naval drones sink Russian warship off Libya’s coast BBC

headline: India's food regulator sanctions prosecution against Bisleri over unsafe water
summary: India's food safety regulator FSSAI sanctioned prosecution on Sunday against packaged water maker Bisleri International after a Goa plant sample exceeded bromate limits and contained polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons. Bisleri countered Monday that its products are safe, saying an approved laboratory found bromate compliant upon independent retesting.
why_it_matters: Targeting a major bottled water maker amid FSSAI crackdowns on food adulteration raises questions over conflicting lab results and chemical safety testing.
source_search: India's food regulator sanctions prosecution against Bisleri over unsafe water Scroll.in

headline: COP31 collapse sparks resignation calls in Australia, Pacific despair
summary: Political fallout erupted Monday after UN COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ended without a final agreement, the first such failure since 2009. The EU rejected a deal omitting fossil fuels under Saudi pressure. Australian opposition lawmakers demanded negotiator Chris Bowen resign, while Pacific island nations voiced despair.
why_it_matters: Failing to secure consensus as global temperatures are set to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius deepens doubts over whether multilateral climate summits can deliver collective action.
source_search: COP31 collapse sparks resignation calls in Australia, Pacific despair Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Tata Steel bids for APL Apollo stake; both stocks slide
summary: Tata Steel announced on Monday a deal worth up to ₹15,511 crore for APL Apollo’s 26.6% promoter stake, plus an open offer for 26% more. The transaction follows Sunday’s ₹28,000-crore asset sale to APL Apollo. Tata Steel shares fell 7.5%, while APL Apollo hit the 20% lower circuit.
why_it_matters: Consolidating 7.5 million tonnes of tubes and colour-coated steel capacity creates a dominant downstream player, though steep cash outflows rattled equity investors.
source_search: Tata Steel bids for APL Apollo stake; both stocks slide The Hindu

headline: Supreme Court sends Saharanpur mosque demolition plea to High Court
summary: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear a contempt plea over the demolition of a 100-year-old mosque in Uttar Pradesh’s Saharanpur, directing Imran Ahmad to approach the Allahabad High Court. Chief Justice Surya Kant’s bench said High Courts must first examine factual violations of its 2024 demolition guidelines.
why_it_matters: Routing bulldozer-related contempt petitions to High Courts signals that enforcement of the Supreme Court’s demolition safeguards will depend on state-level judicial scrutiny.
source_search: Supreme Court sends Saharanpur mosque demolition plea to High Court The Hindu

headline: Alice Huang contacted Chinese spy officer during Nvidia affair: NYT
summary: Alice Huang contacted a Chinese intelligence officer during her affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported Sunday. US officials are investigating her ex-firm Megaspeed over alleged AI chip smuggling, though intelligence chief Jay Clayton said no spying conclusion has been reached.
why_it_matters: Fresh scrutiny of Nvidia’s past sales through Megaspeed is intensifying bipartisan pressure in Washington over whether US semiconductor export controls against China are strictly enforced.
source_search: Alice Huang contacted Chinese spy officer during Nvidia affair: NYT The Hindu

headline: WazirX, ZebPay confirm user data exposed in MoEngage vendor breach
summary: Indian crypto exchanges WazirX and ZebPay disclosed on November 23 that user emails, contact identifiers, and device metadata were exposed in SaaS firm MoEngage's cloud breach. Attackers used a compromised third-party vendor account to access MoEngage's infrastructure, though both exchanges confirmed customer wallets, funds, and trading systems remain safe.
why_it_matters: Supply-chain breaches through smaller third-party vendors are becoming a primary entry point into enterprise infrastructure, especially as AI enables attackers to scale reconnaissance and target multiple organisations simultaneously.
source_search: WazirX, ZebPay confirm user data exposed in MoEngage vendor breach Inc42

headline: S&P projects 7% India growth, sees El Nino driving food inflation
summary: S&P Global Ratings projected Monday that India's GDP will grow 7% in the current and next fiscal years. However, S&P warned that El Nino and uneven rains will stoke food inflation, prompting the Reserve Bank of India to raise policy rates by 25 basis points in December.
why_it_matters: Retail inflation breached the central bank's 6% ceiling in October, meaning higher borrowing costs could dampen household spending even as exports and public investment support headline growth.
source_search: S&P projects 7% India growth, sees El Nino driving food inflation Hindu BusinessLine

headline: India captain Gill urges ICC to restore saliva ball-shining after draw
summary: India captain Shubman Gill urged the ICC to lift its 2020 ban on using saliva to shine balls following a Test draw against New Zealand in Wellington. India scored 720 for 9 after New Zealand made 386, hurting both sides' push for next June's World Test Championship final.
why_it_matters: Restoring saliva polishing could give bowlers more swing, making flat pitches more competitive and helping teams force decisive results in Test cricket.
source_search: India captain Gill urges ICC to restore saliva ball-shining after draw BBC Sport

headline: Bisleri disputes FSSAI prosecution sanction, calls packaged water safe
summary: Bisleri International declared its packaged water safe on Monday, disputing an FSSAI prosecution sanction announced Sunday over a September 2025 Goa plant sample. While initial tests flagged 12 micrograms per litre of bromate, a referral lab cleared bromate but detected PAHs. Bisleri says it received no official notice.
why_it_matters: Conflicting laboratory findings and communication gaps between India’s food safety regulator and a major bottled-water brand raise questions over testing consistency and consumer safety enforcement.
source_search: Bisleri disputes FSSAI prosecution sanction, calls packaged water safe The Hindu

headline: Drones hit UN building in residential area of Sudan’s Khartoum
summary: Drones struck a residential area in Khartoum early Sunday, damaging a UN building and destroying a house without reported casualties. A Sudanese army source alleged the drones came from Ethiopia, which Addis Ababa denies. Drone strikes killed over 1,100 people in Sudan during this year’s first six months.
why_it_matters: Escalating drone warfare inside residential zones endangers humanitarian workers and risks widening Sudan’s conflict through recurring cross-border accusations against neighbouring Ethiopia.
source_search: Drones hit UN building in residential area of Sudan’s Khartoum DW

headline: Meta faces protests in India after content restrictions surge 131-fold
summary: Indian Youth Congress workers protested outside Meta India offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai, and Gurugram, alleging political bias in opposition Instagram account removals. Meta restricted 5.44 million items in India between January and June 2026, a 131-fold surge after New Delhi tightened takedown deadlines to three hours.
why_it_matters: Rapid automated enforcement to meet three-hour legal takedown windows often leaves users without clear legal citations, intensifying scrutiny over algorithmic moderation in one of Meta's biggest compliance markets.
source_search: Meta faces protests in India after content restrictions surge 131-fold Inc42

headline: India private sector growth hits five-month high on factory surge
summary: HSBC's Flash India Composite PMI hit a projected five-month high of 56.3 in November, up from 56.2 in October, data showed Monday. Factory output jumped to 58.3 while services eased to 55.3. Stronger foreign demand lifted export orders to a four-month high, boosting year-ahead business optimism.
why_it_matters: Broad expansion across pharmaceuticals, electronics, chemicals, and infrastructure signals resilient private-sector demand well above the 50-point growth threshold despite moderating services activity.
source_search: India private sector growth hits five-month high on factory surge Livemint

headline: De Villiers alleges Australia tampered with ball in 2018 Durban Test
summary: Former South Africa batter AB de Villiers alleged on YouTube that Australia tampered with the ball in the 2018 Durban series opener, not only later Tests. Australia's bowlers and then coach Darren Lehmann deny knowledge, while Cricket Australia launched a voluntary forum carrying no new penalties.
why_it_matters: Fresh testimony widening the sandpaper scandal to Australia's Durban win puts renewed pressure on current captain Pat Cummins and Cricket Australia's leadership.
source_search: De Villiers alleges Australia tampered with ball in 2018 Durban Test BBC Sport

headline: Elizabeth Holmes documentary breaks UK box office opening weekend record
summary: A24's three-hour Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything" grossed $3.2 million across 596 UK and Ireland cinemas following its Nov. 20 release. Directed by Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder, it surpassed "Fahrenheit 9/11" for the biggest non-concert documentary opening there after topping $90 million in the US.
why_it_matters: Record pre-sales and 790 sold-out theatres demonstrate that pent-up word-of-mouth demand can turn traditional non-fiction cinema into a major wide-release theatrical draw.
source_search: Elizabeth Holmes documentary breaks UK box office opening weekend record Variety

headline: NHS launches world's largest trial of AI breast cancer screening
summary: The NHS has launched the EDITH trial at Cambridge University Hospitals, inviting nearly 700,000 UK women across 30 sites to test AI in breast cancer screening. AI will replace one of two human mammogram readers, aiming to improve early cancer detection and ease radiologist shortfalls without unnecessary overdiagnosis.
why_it_matters: With imaging examinations rising 8% annually amid a radiologist shortfall, proving AI accuracy at scale could free specialists to treat patients sooner.
source_search: NHS launches world's largest trial of AI breast cancer screening BBC

headline: Chief Justice Surya Kant recuses himself from Supertech insolvency plea
summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday recused himself from a Supertech insolvency plea after noting an applicant was known to him, saying a special bench will hear it. The dispute affects state-run NBCC’s court-backed plan to finish 16 stalled housing projects covering 49,748 homes.
why_it_matters: Constituting a new bench prolongs legal uncertainty for tens of thousands of homebuyers who have waited nearly two decades for Supertech apartment deliveries.
source_search: Chief Justice Surya Kant recuses himself from Supertech insolvency plea The Hindu

headline: Israeli opposition leader condemns West Bank arson as ‘Jewish terrorism’
summary: Israeli authorities investigated Sunday’s pre-dawn settler arson attacks that torched around eight Palestinian vehicles and defaced homes across four West Bank towns. The military condemned the vandalism and deployed forces. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, currently negotiating a post-election coalition, denounced the violence as Jewish terrorism and demanded severe sanctions.
why_it_matters: Growing political willingness in Israel to label settler violence as terrorism reflects warnings that extremist attacks undermine regional stability, national security, and foreign relations.
source_search: Israeli opposition leader condemns West Bank arson as ‘Jewish terrorism’ DW

headline: Microsoft, US intelligence warn of more major tech outages ahead
summary: Microsoft President Brad Smith and US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned of further major tech disruptions following recent FAA, Outlook, and JPMorgan Chase outages. Speaking on CBS and CNN, both officials noted that sweeping infrastructure upgrades and AI-assisted vulnerability discovery will cause months of instability.
why_it_matters: Whether caused by rushed software patching or AI-accelerated hackers, prolonged outages across aviation, banking, and enterprise email expose how fragile aging global digital infrastructure has become.
source_search: Microsoft, US intelligence warn of more major tech outages ahead The Verge

headline: Mamata's TMC accuses rebel faction of forging Election Commission affidavits
summary: Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress faction filed a Kolkata police complaint accusing breakaway leaders Arup Roy and Ritabrata Banerjee of forging affidavits with police help before the Election Commission. Roughly 60 of 80 TMC MLAs defected after May's loss, leaving both groups contesting the frozen party symbol.
why_it_matters: Criminal allegations over forged voter-roll affidavits complicate the Election Commission's court-ordered four-month deadline to rule on control of West Bengal's former ruling party.
source_search: Mamata's TMC accuses rebel faction of forging Election Commission affidavits Scroll.in

headline: US Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $1.8 billion as seven-week slump deepens
summary: Investors pulled $1.8 billion from 12 US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs last week, marking the fourth straight week of withdrawals and the steepest exit since June. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust saw a record $544 million Friday outflow as Bitcoin endured a seventh consecutive weekly drop before steadying above $61,000 Monday.
why_it_matters: With over $3.7 billion withdrawn this year following October's $6 billion Binance hack and higher US rate expectations, institutional ETF demand is no longer cushioning crypto volatility.
source_search: US Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $1.8 billion as seven-week slump deepens Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Swindon Town sack manager Ian Holloway after fourth straight defeat
summary: Swindon Town sacked manager Ian Holloway after Saturday's 2-0 League Two loss at Newport County left them 17th with four consecutive defeats. Appointed in October 2024, Holloway won just two of his last 15 matches; coaches Gavin Gunning and Steve Mildenhall take interim charge with David Carney assisting.
why_it_matters: Having missed promotion last season and scored once in five league games, Swindon's chronic injuries and stagnation mean a managerial change offers no quick fix.
source_search: Swindon Town sack manager Ian Holloway after fourth straight defeat BBC Sport

headline: Thriller 'White Blast' tops South Korean box office, ending 'Chiikawa' streak
summary: Showbox's local mystery thriller "White Blast" opened atop South Korea's box office over Nov. 20 to 22, earning $2.3 million across 1,244 screens for a 39.6% share. The debut ended Japanese anime "Chiikawa the Movie"'s five-week streak at first, though "Chiikawa" crossed three million total admissions.
why_it_matters: A local stage adaptation claiming nearly 40% of weekend receipts shows domestic thrillers can still reclaim Korean multiplexes from imported franchise hits.
source_search: Thriller 'White Blast' tops South Korean box office, ending 'Chiikawa' streak Variety

headline: Northern Ireland consultants begin 24-hour strike in pay dispute
summary: Northern Ireland consultants and specialist doctors began a 24-hour strike at 07:00 GMT Monday, following Friday's resident doctor walkout over pay. The British Medical Association rejected a 3.5% raise, demanding 2008 pay parity. Health Minister Robbie Butler warned the combined strikes will disrupt care for roughly 1,694 patients.
why_it_matters: Rescheduling cancelled procedures ahead of winter strains an already pressured health budget, while ministers warn higher doctor pay could trigger wider public-sector demands.
source_search: Northern Ireland consultants begin 24-hour strike in pay dispute BBC
